all_verified_current.title: Adulterated and misbranded drug prohibition
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Federal law prohibits dispensing or distributing adulterated or misbranded drugs; labeling, strength, purity, storage, and manufacturing defects can trigger different statutory classifications.

all_verified_current.title: Follow-up after emergency oral Schedule II dispensing
all_verified_current.rule_summary: The prescriber must deliver the required written or electronic follow-up Schedule II prescription to the pharmacy within seven days after authorizing emergency oral dispensing.

all_verified_current.title: Emergency oral Schedule II prescription requirements
all_verified_current.rule_summary: In a defined emergency, a pharmacist may dispense an oral Schedule II prescription only in the quantity necessary for the emergency period after immediate communication with and reasonable identification of the prescriber.

all_verified_current.title: Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Federal law prohibits refilling a Schedule II prescription; additional dispensing requires a new lawful prescription or a permitted remainder of a partial fill.

all_verified_current.title: Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability
all_verified_current.rule_summary: When a Schedule II prescription is partially filled because the pharmacy cannot supply the full quantity, the remaining portion must generally be supplied within 72 hours or the pharmacist must notify the prescriber and obtain a new prescription for further quantity.

all_verified_current.title: Patient-requested Schedule II partial fill
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Schedule II prescription may be partially filled at the patient or prescriber request when state law permits, with the remaining portion dispensed no later than 30 days after the prescription was written unless a shorter applicable limit controls.

all_verified_current.title: Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after its issue date and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.

all_verified_current.title: Federal partial filling of Schedule III through V prescriptions
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Schedule III through V prescription may be partially filled if each partial fill is recorded like a refill, the total does not exceed the prescribed quantity, and dispensing occurs within six months after issue.

all_verified_current.title: Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.

all_verified_current.title: Federal controlled-substance schedules
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Federal controlled-substance classifications are established in 21 CFR Part 1308; drug-specific questions must cite the exact applicable schedule section rather than an undifferentiated omnibus reference.

all_verified_current.title: Federal controlled-substance record retention
all_verified_current.rule_summary: DEA-required controlled-substance inventories and records must be maintained and available for inspection for at least two years unless another provision requires longer.

all_verified_current.title: Controlled Substance Ordering System electronic orders
all_verified_current.rule_summary: CSOS permits a properly credentialed registrant or authorized subscriber to issue digitally signed electronic Schedule I and II orders in place of paper DEA Form 222.

all_verified_current.title: Non-retrievable standard for controlled-substance destruction
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Controlled substances destroyed by a registrant must be rendered non-retrievable so their physical or chemical condition is permanently altered and unavailable for practical use.

all_verified_current.title: One-time transfer of electronic controlled prescriptions
all_verified_current.rule_summary: At a patient's request, an unfilled electronic Schedule II through V prescription may be transferred once between DEA-registered retail pharmacies if allowed by state law, kept electronic, unaltered, and communicated directly between pharmacists.

all_verified_current.title: DEA Form 222 validity and partial shipments
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A supplier may make partial shipments on an accepted DEA Form 222 during the 60-day period after execution; the form is generally invalid after 60 days.

all_verified_current.title: Defective DEA Form 222 may not be corrected
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A supplier may not fill an incomplete, illegible, improperly executed, altered, or erased DEA Form 222; a defective form cannot be corrected and must be replaced.

all_verified_current.title: Lost or stolen DEA Form 222 reporting
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A registrant must immediately report lost or stolen used or unused DEA Forms 222 to the responsible DEA Special Agent in Charge and retain the required replacement-form statements.

all_verified_current.title: Schedule I and II ordering by Form 222 or CSOS
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A distribution of Schedule I or II controlled substances generally requires a DEA Form 222 or a compliant digitally signed electronic order unless a listed exception applies.

all_verified_current.title: DEA Form 222 preservation
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Paper DEA Form 222 records must be maintained separately for two years; electronic Form 222 records are deemed separately maintained when they are readily retrievable from other records.

all_verified_current.title: Controlled-substance destruction records
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A registrant that destroys or causes destruction of controlled substances must maintain the required destruction record, generally using DEA Form 41, with the required substance, method, place, date, and witness information.

all_verified_current.title: Biennial controlled-substance inventory
all_verified_current.rule_summary: After the initial inventory, each registrant must take a new controlled-substance inventory at least every two years.

all_verified_current.title: Exact and estimated controlled-substance inventory counts
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Schedule II inventory requires an exact count or measure; Schedule III through V opened containers may generally be estimated unless the container holds more than 1,000 units.

all_verified_current.title: Initial controlled-substance inventory
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A newly registered handler must take an inventory of controlled substances on hand on the date first engaging in controlled-substance activity.

all_verified_current.title: FDA Medication Guide distribution
all_verified_current.rule_summary: When FDA requires a Medication Guide for a product, the authorized dispenser must provide it under the conditions in 21 CFR Part 208, subject to the regulation's exceptions.

all_verified_current.title: Prescription drug sample restrictions
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Prescription drug samples are distributed only through the authorized practitioner and manufacturer or distributor pathways; a pharmacy may not treat samples marked not for resale as ordinary saleable inventory.

all_verified_current.title: Federal pseudoephedrine retail quantity limits
all_verified_current.rule_summary: For ordinary non-mail-order retail sales, federal CMEA rules limit pseudoephedrine base to 3.6 grams per purchaser per day and 9 grams per purchaser during a 30-day period.

all_verified_current.title: Drug recall segregation and response
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy follows the recall notice and lot-specific instructions, removes affected stock from availability, preserves traceability, and does not assume every recall requires every patient to stop therapy immediately.

all_verified_current.title: Product-specific FDA REMS requirements
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy dispensing a drug subject to an FDA REMS must follow the current product-specific certification, authorization, documentation, and safe-use requirements that apply to the dispenser.

all_verified_current.title: Transfer to a registered reverse distributor
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A registrant may transfer controlled substances to a DEA-registered reverse distributor under the applicable inventory, ordering, transfer, and record requirements.

all_verified_current.title: Federal reporting of significant controlled-substance theft or loss
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A DEA registrant must notify the responsible DEA field division in writing within one business day after discovering a theft or significant loss and complete the required electronic DEA Form 106 process.

all_verified_current.title: Retail CDTM Schedule II through V prohibition
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A retail collaborative practice agreement may not authorize the pharmacist to prescribe Schedule II through V controlled substances.

all_verified_current.title: Pharmacist qualifications for collaborative drug therapy management
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A collaborating pharmacist must satisfy Massachusetts licensure, experience or degree, liability insurance, practice-focus, and additional annual continuing-education requirements.

all_verified_current.title: Retail collaborative drug therapy management scope
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Retail CDTM is limited to referred and consenting adults, the diseases and actions authorized by statute, the supervising physician's agreement, and other statutory setting restrictions.

all_verified_current.title: Retail CDTM Schedule VI prescribing
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A properly authorized retail collaborating pharmacist may issue Schedule VI prescriptions for the referred diagnosis and must send a copy to the supervising physician within 24 hours.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts compounding continuing education
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacist overseeing or directly engaged in covered sterile or complex nonsterile compounding must complete the applicable additional annual compounding continuing-education hours.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts Schedule II and III single-fill quantity framework
all_verified_current.subtopic: Schedule II and III quantity limits
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps.

all_verified_current.title: Patient option to request a lesser Schedule II quantity
all_verified_current.rule_summary: At the patient's request, a Massachusetts pharmacist may dispense less than the prescribed Schedule II quantity and document the partial fill in the patient record.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts patient-requested Schedule II partial fill
all_verified_current.rule_summary: For the Massachusetts patient-requested Schedule II partial-fill pathway, the initial partial dispensing and later remainder are subject to statutory timing and same-pharmacy conditions.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts Schedule II patient-request remainder
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Only the pharmacy that made the initial patient-requested Schedule II partial fill may dispense the remainder, and the remainder must be filled no later than 30 days after issue.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts Schedule II prescription validity
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II prescription becomes invalid 30 days after its issue date.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts electronic-prescribing requirement
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Massachusetts generally requires covered prescriptions to be issued electronically subject to 105 CMR 721.070 exceptions and waivers. Schedule VI prescriptions are excepted from the state electronic-prescribing requirement under 105 CMR 721.070(A)(9). Under 105 CMR 721.070(C), a pharmacist who receives an otherwise valid written or oral prescription is not required to verify that the prescription properly falls within an electronic-prescribing exception or waiver; all other prescription and controlled-substance requirements still apply.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts patient counseling
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacist must comply with the patient-counseling requirements of 247 CMR 9.18, including a meaningful offer or provision in the settings and circumstances governed by the regulation.

all_verified_current.title: Pharmacy continuous quality improvement program
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Each pharmacy must maintain a continuous quality improvement program that detects, documents, assesses, and prevents quality-related events.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts pharmacy controlled-substance security
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Massachusetts pharmacy must maintain controlled substances securely and comply with the storage, access, accountability, and loss-response requirements in 247 CMR 9.21 and applicable federal law.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts Schedule V prescription refill limits
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Massachusetts Schedule V prescription may not be refilled more than five times or later than six months after the prescription was issued.

all_verified_current.title: Pharmacist prescribing of hormonal contraception
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Massachusetts pharmacist may prescribe and dispense eligible hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral products after the required screening and under the official protocol and labeling.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts interchangeable-drug dispensing
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacist dispenses a less expensive reasonably available interchangeable product listed under Massachusetts standards unless the prescriber validly indicates no substitution or another exception applies.

all_verified_current.title: Daily pharmacy internship credit limit
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy intern may receive no more than 12 hours of pharmacy internship credit in one day.

all_verified_current.title: Direct supervision of Massachusetts pharmacy interns
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern works under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor.

all_verified_current.title: Licensee demographic and status reporting
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Board licensees must update specified contact information and report specified name, criminal, disciplinary, or certification events within the applicable 14-day reporting period.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts naloxone prescribing and dispensing
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Naloxone may lawfully be prescribed and dispensed to a person at risk or to another person positioned to assist, and Massachusetts pharmacy pathways include standing-order and reporting provisions.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts initial opioid seven-day limit
all_verified_current.rule_summary: An initial outpatient opiate prescription for an adult and any opiate prescription for a minor is generally limited to seven days, subject to documented statutory exceptions; opioid-dependence treatment is excluded.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts oral Schedule III through V follow-up request
all_verified_current.rule_summary: For an oral Schedule III through V prescription issued under the out-of-state pathway, the pharmacist records requesting a written prescription within seven days or the shorter federal period.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts dispensing of out-of-state Schedule II prescriptions
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Massachusetts applies a five-day presentation window and different issuing-state conditions to out-of-state narcotic and nonnarcotic Schedule II prescriptions.

all_verified_current.title: Out-of-state Schedule II narcotic prescriptions
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Massachusetts may fill a Schedule II narcotic prescription from Maine or a contiguous state within five days of issue after required authentication and verification; separate delivery provisions govern certain out-of-state residents.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts pharmacist continuing education
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A renewing pharmacist generally completes 20 contact hours in each calendar year of the two-year cycle, including at least two hours of pharmacy law each year, with limits on home study and daily credit.

all_verified_current.title: Controlled substances and credentials after pharmacy closure
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Within 14 days after closure, the resident pharmacy submits original licenses and controlled-substance registration plus an attestation of lawful controlled-substance disposal or transfer.

all_verified_current.title: Advance Board notice of pharmacy closure
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A resident pharmacy generally must give the Board written certified-mail notice at least 14 days before intended closure and provide the required closure and controlled-substance information.

all_verified_current.title: Patient notice before pharmacy closure
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A closing pharmacy identifies patients served in the preceding 90 days, attempts notice at least 14 days before closure, posts conspicuous notice, and supports timely patient-file transfer.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts pharmacy MassPAT dispensing-data reporting
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.

all_verified_current.title: Prospective drug utilization review
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Before dispensing, a pharmacist must perform the prospective drug utilization review required by 247 CMR 9.17 and resolve clinically significant issues through professional judgment and communication.

all_verified_current.title: Quality-related event analysis and systems response
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy must analyze quality-related events for causes and contributing workflow, technology, training, and staffing factors and use the findings to improve systems and processes.

all_verified_current.title: Annual CQI education for pharmacy personnel
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy's CQI program must provide ongoing education in continuous quality improvement to pharmacy personnel at least annually.

all_verified_current.title: Quality-related event documentation deadline
all_verified_current.rule_summary: The pharmacist who discovers or receives notice of a quality-related event must initially document it within 24 hours after discovery or notification.

all_verified_current.title: Immediate response after discovery of a quality-related event
all_verified_current.rule_summary: On discovery of a quality-related event, the pharmacist must immediately notify the patient or representative, notify the prescriber when professionally indicated, and give corrective and harm-minimization directions.

all_verified_current.title: Returned erroneous or defective medication quarantine
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy accepts medication it dispensed in error or that is suspected defective or contaminated, but may not return it to inventory and must quarantine and properly dispose of it.

all_verified_current.title: Out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescriptions
all_verified_current.rule_summary: An authorized out-of-state practitioner may issue a Schedule III through VI prescription filled in Massachusetts within 30 days of issue; Schedule III through V prescriptions require pharmacist verification.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts controlled-prescription retention
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy keeps controlled-substance prescriptions for two years and makes them available for inspection under Massachusetts law.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts controlled-prescription required elements
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A controlled-substance prescription must include the practitioner, patient, drug, strength, directions, date, registration, cautionary, and refill information required by Massachusetts law.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts transfer of prescriptions
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Under current 247 CMR 9.14, a pharmacy must timely transfer a prescription at the request of the patient or authorized agent, may act as the patient's agent to obtain the transfer, and may not charge a transfer fee. Schedule VI prescriptions transfer in the same manner as Schedule III-V prescriptions; remaining authorized refills may be transferred, but a Schedule VI prescription may not be transferred more than one year after issuance. Under 247 CMR 8.04, a certified pharmacy technician may perform a Schedule VI transfer with approval of the pharmacist on duty.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Massachusetts Schedule VI includes prescription drugs not otherwise placed in Schedules I through V; Schedule VI status does not itself make a drug federally controlled or routinely MassPAT-reportable.

all_verified_current.title: Retention of serious-event reporting records
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A pharmacy must retain readily retrievable records relating to reportable improper dispensing and serious adverse drug events for at least five years from filing the report.

all_verified_current.title: Reporting improper dispensing and serious adverse drug events
all_verified_current.rule_summary: A manager of record must report qualifying improper dispensing with serious injury or death and qualifying serious adverse drug events within seven business days of discovery or employee knowledge.

all_verified_current.title: Schedule II handling by pharmacy support personnel
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.05, a pharmacy intern may handle Schedule II controlled substances under direct pharmacist supervision; an ordinary pharmacy technician may assist with transporting Schedule II substances, while a certified pharmacy technician may assist with transporting and handling them when the pharmacist supervises and approves the activity and written policies and procedures govern it. Pharmacist professional judgment is not delegated.

all_verified_current.title: Massachusetts pharmacy technician scope and pharmacist responsibility
all_verified_current.rule_summary: Pharmacy technicians and trainees may perform only duties allowed by 247 CMR 8 under pharmacist supervision; judgmental pharmacist functions may not be delegated.

used_twice.rule_summary: A pharmacy accepts medication it dispensed in error or that is suspected defective or contaminated, but may not return it to inventory and must quarantine and properly dispose of it.

used_twice.title: Massachusetts controlled-prescription retention
used_twice.rule_summary: A pharmacy keeps controlled-substance prescriptions for two years and makes them available for inspection under Massachusetts law.

used_twice.title: Retention of serious-event reporting records
used_twice.rule_summary: A pharmacy must retain readily retrievable records relating to reportable improper dispensing and serious adverse drug events for at least five years from filing the report.

used_twice.title: Schedule II handling by pharmacy support personnel
used_twice.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.05, a pharmacy intern may handle Schedule II controlled substances under direct pharmacist supervision; an ordinary pharmacy technician may assist with transporting Schedule II substances, while a certified pharmacy technician may assist with transporting and handling them when the pharmacist supervises and approves the activity and written policies and procedures govern it. Pharmacist professional judgment is not delegated.
